Another motion with respect to Osman Kadic, the 12th of July, 2006, the translation handed over the 13th of February. No response from the accused. And a report by Mr. Andras Riedlmayer, 23rd of May, 2006, that is the oldest, it is almost nine months ago, and the translation was addressed on the 10th of October. No response from Mr. Seselj. Therefore, to summarise, regarding all the expert reports, with the exception of Oberschall, which has no translation, all the others have been translated, there's a blockade because Mr. Seselj has not taken note of them and he cannot convey his position as a result. Mr. Seselj, will you confirm that that is your position?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Antonetti. I believe that I did file a number of submissions in this set of 14 that relate to expert reports that have not been disclosed to me in response to introductory submissions by the Prosecution. This is obviously evidence of ill-will and ill-intentions because this is easiest for them to put on paper. They have the translations, the originals, either in Serbian or in English or French. In any event, they have the translations, but all this is on CDs, and they find it difficult to put this on paper, and this entails the job of one day. These are not audio-recordings requiring more time; it is simply a question of printing them out and handing them to me. They could have done this almost a year ago, and they still haven't. Because, again, they hope that someone may rule to impose Defence counsel, to impose electronic documents, to impose documents in English. I don't know what they're expecting, but in any event they're not doing anything about it. I wish to contest all the expert reports and to prepare a counter-report with the main thesis for my contesting those submissions, and I would like to cross-examine all those experts, although they requested 92 bis for Ivan Grujic, that is his expert report, in another case. I insist that I have the opportunity to cross-examine each of those experts, and I will challenge the expert reports, of course, as soon as I receive those reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, the question of these reports has been more clearly clarified on page 49 onwards. You have told us that your intention is to cross-examine all the experts. All this is very clear now. I will give you the floor, Mr. Saxon, but just a technical detail, Mr. Seselj. I have understood the question of CDs, CD-ROMs. You are telling us: I do wish to examine the content of the reports, but I need to have them in hard copy. Very well. But my understanding was that the registrar gave you a person, a case manager, precisely to deal with these specific concrete problems. Could it not be a solution for the person who has been assigned to this job to receive this CD-ROM, to put it in his or her computer, press a button, and print out the document, and then you have it in hard copy. Would it not be possible to work in this way?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This person, Mr. Antonetti, does not exist. You have been misinformed. If you held in mind the case manager, as he is known here, he does not have this as part of his duties. And I know this with certainty because I personally compiled his work assignments and handed it to the registry, and they can confirm this. This is really a very small job that the Prosecution or a member of the registry can do, rather than a member of my Defence. This is an additional burden on the Defence, which has incomparably less facilities than the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, are you telling me that you haven't yet met the case manager? You haven't seen him?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't say that. You must have a bad translation. Of course, I've seen this person. I know this person for 10 or 15 years, and I have full confidence in her, and that is why I appointed her, but that is not part of her duties. It is not part of the job she has. She does an enormous amount of work for me currently in Belgrade because she cannot live on the small salary she has been given here, and she cannot give up her job in Belgrade. She is also a member of parliament there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. I understand now. I will discuss this again with the registrar, but regardless of this assignment that you gave to this case manager and who's working with you, as you have known her for many years, I thought that someone has been put at your disposal to fulfil these simple concrete tasks, and I now realise that that is not the case. Thank you anyway for the clarifications you have given, which makes it easier for us to get a full grasp of the problem. Mr. Saxon, on expert reports or anything else, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just very briefly with regard to the subject of expert reports, the Prosecution would like to inform the Chamber that it expects to provide an addendum to the expert report of military analyst Reynaud Theunens, because the Prosecution has received additional material related to Mr. Theunens' original report recently that require additional discussion in his report. It is also possible, Your Honour, that the Prosecution may submit an addendum to the expert report of Mr. Yves Tomic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You have now informed Mr. Seselj and the Chamber of these additional addendums. I think -- yes. Yes, Mr. Seselj. For the addendums to the expert reports, about that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as addendums are concerned, I have received the report of Yvo Tomic or Yves Tomic. I presume he's a Frenchman, so I'm not quite sure how to pronounce his name. I have prepared a response by my legal assistants and I have tried to hand it over, and they returned it twice. I will hand it in a third time. But I hear for the first time about a report by a Mr. Theunens, and now I hear that there will be an addendum to his report. They haven't even tried to inform me yet about such an expert report. In -- I have been informed about these five, that they exist, but I haven't received them because they are in electronic form, but I hear about Theunens for the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honour, the redacted version of the expert report of Mr. Theunens was filed on the 31st of March, 2006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, since the 31st of March, 2006, that's almost for a year, you must have had this report?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if I may, Your Honour, a decision was issued by the former Trial Chamber on the 2nd of October, 2006, to provide this material to the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But why hasn't this been handed over to me? Why haven't I received it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apparently, Mr. Seselj hasn't received the decision of the 2nd of October, 2006. In that case, I will look into this matter and refer to it next time. I will close with the last motion. It is a motion of a third party, two accused in another case wish to have access to the testimony and documents of this case. There was a motion on the 10th of January, 2007. The Prosecution has responded to it. The translation was transmitted to Mr. Seselj on the 11th of January, 2007, and the position of the Prosecution also to the -- on the 22nd of January, 2007. So, Mr. Seselj, you also need to respond to these motions and express your opinion about them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can recollect, this is a request of the Prosecution for the Defence of Gotovina, Markac, Cermak have insight into the file of my case. Can Mr. Saxon confirm this or deny it? Am I right? Am I right, that that is what is involved before I state an opinion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's not a motion from the Prosecution. It is a motion from the Defence of Cermak and Markac who wish to have access to the file, and the Prosecution has asked for this to be rejected. So we are talking about the same cases. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I didn't get it right. I just wanted to hear whether we are talking about this case. I have received this motion and the response of the Prosecution, but I'm quite indifferent. I do not oppose or accept it. I have no interest in it either way. My interests are not in jeopardy in any way if their Defence has insight into the case before me, into my trial in other case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. So your position has been registered, recorded. We will shortly be adjourning. First of all, I wish to say to the Prosecution, who have given us an indictment which is in agreement with a ruling, and the request of Mr. Seselj, when he said there were lots of blackened out paragraphs. So this has been corrected, and the Prosecution has also provided a list of witnesses, an updated list. Isn't that so, Mr. Saxon? I am not mistaken on these two points, am I?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Antonetti.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I still haven't received this, unfortunately. I probably will if it's ready, but I have something very important to raise in some detail today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As we are now under miscellaneous, I give you the floor. You may raise the issue you wanted to raise.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can't change the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, but I hope I can express the fact that I don't agree with Rule 92 quater, a recently introduced rule, which makes it possible for the dead to testify before this court. That probably tallies with Western legal practice. I know that Western legal practice also recognises the possibility of putting the dead on trial. So the dead can also be accused. In 897, the Pope, Steven the VII, ordered that his predecessor the Pope Formosus, should be excavated, should be dug out of his grave, he should be put on trial and sentenced to death at the stake. Recently an illegal Irish court sentenced the dead Slobodan Milosevic to 30 years in prison. Amicus curiae, Stephen Kay participated in the case. He was later imposed as counsel for Milosevic and there was also a lawyer from Belgrade, et cetera. So such a legal practice exists in the West, but something has happened in my case, something that I haven't come across in Western legal practice that I reject in disgust. On the 16th of March of this year, I received a Prosecution's submission with an up-to-date list of exhibits and an annex. It's partially confidential. Whatever is confidential, I will not mention. I would like to point that out so you don't feel the need to move into private session. The Prosecution filed it on the 17th of November, 2006. 3.349 exhibits were listed on 375 pages. Almost 10 per cent of the exhibits, exhibits the Prosecution wants to have admitted through the deceased Milan Babic and his testimony. 334 -- 335 exhibits in total. I apologise. They're not all in the same place. I had gathered this information together. The Prosecution from the death -- the time when Milan Babic died up until the 17th of November had a lot of time to introduce these exhibits through some other witnesses. There are many exhibits that they wanted to tender through other dead witnesses who are protected, so I won't even mention their names. I think this has never been seen in a Western legal practice to date. Trials of the dead are allowed and it's possible to use the testimony of the dead. How are they going to use the deceased Milan Babic to have over 305 exhibits tendered into evidence? I believe you have this document before you. You can see this for yourself. In this pre-trial phase, I think that it's important for you as the Pre-Trial Judge to adopt a position as far as this matter is concerned and for the Trial Chamber to do so, too. And if possible, if you accept this, allow me to file an appeal because this can't be accepted. You can't have 305 exhibits tendered through the testimony of the deceased Milan Babic and how do you intend to do this? Could you explain that to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Saxon, you will respond, but before you do so, I'd like to clarify something for Mr. Seselj. 92 bis or quater allows for the written statement of someone to be admitted even if he is dead, but there is a paragraph (B) that I will read out to you slowly now. It reads as follows: "If the evidence goes to proof of acts and conduct of an accused as charged in the indictment, this may be a factor against the admission of such evidence or that part of it." So the Rule that was drafted provides for the admission of the written statements of people who now are deceased, but the Chamber that has to rule on a Prosecution motion must examine the case and see whether the testimony concerns acts and conduct of an individual. And if that is the case, the Chamber will decide whether such testimony should be admitted or not. So that is what is provided for by Article 92 quater.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Antonetti, may I add something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are quite right, but we are talking about tendering documents into evidence through the testimony of a dead witness, because the Prosecution quite clearly states in this document, the documents are being tendered through the testimony of Milan Babic, so the testimony of Milan Babic in other cases is one matter, his previous statements and his plea agreement is one matter. But tendering exhibits into evidence in this way is another matter, because 305 exhibits represents 10 per cent of the exhibits that the Prosecution has in mind. These exhibits involve various documents that in principle have nothing to do with Milan Babic. So how can these 305 documents be tendered through his testimony? This is what is not clear to me, and this is something that is not provided for in the Rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Saxon, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution's position is that exhibits that were tendered through -- discussed by a witness, such as the witness in question, Milan Babic, are part of that witness's prior testimony. The accused may not be aware that on the 12th of March, the Prosecution filed a motion under Rule 92 quater seeking the admission of the prior testimony and number of exhibits that were discussed by the witness during his prior testimony. It may be that the Prosecution's motion has not been translated yet into the accused's language, but when it is I assume it will be formally filed, and then the accused will have an opportunity to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, apparently there is a Prosecution document dated the 12th of March that it appears you have not yet received or you have not yet received the translation of that document. When you do, you'll be in a better position to respond. But I have taken note of the legal arguments you made on page 56, the arguments that concern the problem as to whether this procedure allows for the 305 documents to be admitted into evidence. It is now time to adjourn. Mr. Seselj, are there any other issues you would like to address? If not, I have to put certain questions to you --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one sentence, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saxon hasn't responded to your question. I received requests from the Prosecution to have Milan Babic's testimony admitted pursuant to 92 quater, but the Prosecution's request to have exhibits from other cases admitted is one thing, and a list of exhibits from my case is another thing. I'm referring to the list of exhibits from my case, a list that the Prosecution provided on over 300 pages. In this case, I didn't mention taking over exhibits from other cases. It seems that the Prosecution needs a lesson in elementary law. You have understood my objection, but the Prosecution didn't want to respond to it. They've mentioned something else, some other problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But perhaps the Prosecution, by not responding, reserved for itself the possibility of providing a more detailed response or perhaps they believe that the written submissions show that a Chamber can admit these 305 documents. But the Trial Chamber will rule on this. I cannot now tell you what the Chamber's position will be. Mr. Seselj, I believe you have no other issues to address. According to the Rules, I must put the following question to you. Are the detention conditions fine? Do you have any complaints to make? Or is everything all right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, nothing is wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saxon, is there anything else you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will now adjourn. I would like to thank everyone. You have all participated in the dialogue I'm trying to establish. Both parties have expressed their positions. Mr. Seselj, you were very clear and precise in what you said, and I'm happy with the atmosphere that has prevailed during the course of this hearing. I hope that the atmosphere will be the same in the upcoming hearings, and once I have taken stock of certain problems with the Registrar, certain problems that have already been mentioned and certain issues raised, I will see you again, certainly within two or three weeks' time. So we will meet again in the very near future, and I think that next time we'll perhaps examine the motions because I think that many solutions will have been found to certain issues. Next time I would like to address the subject of the witnesses who will be called. I would like to see what the schedule is, what we are planning for, and what problems we feel we might encounter. If we can make a precise list of the problems that exist, it will be possible to start with the trial under the best possible conditions. Given that Mr. Seselj is defending himself on his own, there might be certain technical or practical issues to deal with, and I would like to deal with these issues next time we meet. So we will meet each other in the very near future, and I thank you for your participation and for the positive atmosphere that prevailed in the courtroom. Thank you, and I will see you in the very near future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: adjourned at 12.04 p.m.
